summary: Eli Franco is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Charles Malamoud at Paris Nanterre and EPHE, and completed his habilitation at Hamburg. He held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, University of Vienna, and University of Leipzig (2004–2021).

Elijah Sacvan Ary is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sera Monastery under Geshe Karma Sonam, at INALCO, and earned his PhD at Harvard University under Janet Gyatso and Leonard van der Kuijp.

Eliot Deutsch was a philosopher and Indologist who earned his PhD from Columbia University. He served as professor and chair at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (1960–1967) and professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1967–2006), where he also edited Philosophy East and West.

Elisa Freschi is an Indologist and philosopher who earned her doctorate under Raffaele Torella. She held positions at Sapienza University of Rome, the University of Vienna (~2012–2021), and joined the University of Toronto as Associate Professor around 2021.
Elisa Ganser is an Indology scholar. Her attested academic posts in 2026 include Lektorin at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities and visiting researcher at the University of Zurich.

Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza is a religious studies scholar who studied at Würzburg and Münster. She held professorships at the University of Notre Dame (1970–1984), Episcopal Divinity School (1984–1988), and Harvard University (from 1988), and served as president of the Society of Biblical Literature.

Elizabeth A. Cecil works in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. She earned her PhD from Brown University under James L. Fitzgerald. Her career includes posts at the University of Groningen (2011–2013) and Florida State University (attested 2021).

Elizabeth De Michelis is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She completed her master's at SOAS and her PhD at the University of Cambridge, where she served as director in 2000, and later held a post at the University of Oxford.
Elizabeth English is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied under Alexis Sanderson and Harunaga Isaacson, earning her PhD from the University of Oxford in 1999.

Elizabeth Errington is a specialist in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at SOAS under Adrian David Hugh Bivar and served as curator of pre-Islamic coins of South and Central Asia at the British Museum from 1993.

Elizabeth Guthrie is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Canterbury in 1994 and held a post as a tutor in Religious Studies at the University of Otago (attested 2007).

Elizabeth J. Harris specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her doctorate at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under Ananda Guruge and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa. She held posts at Westminster College (~1993–1997) and the University of Birmingham (~2018).

Elizabeth J. Perry is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at the University of Michigan (~1971–1978) and held academic posts at the University of Washington (~1978–1986) and Harvard University (~1997).

Elizabeth Morrison is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She completed doctoral studies under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt, serving as an instructor at Amherst College (1998–1999) and holding an attested post at Middlebury College in 2008.

Elizabeth Napper is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Virginia, studying under Paul Groner, Jeffrey Hopkins, and Geshe Wangyal, and served as co-director of the Tibetan Nuns Project (attested 2001–2006).
Elizabeth Stuart is a religious studies scholar who founded Theology & Sexuality. She served as Direktorin at the University of Winchester in 2021.

Elke Rogersdotter is a scholar in archaeology and Indology. She completed her PhD at Umeå University (attested 2006) under the supervision of Thomas B. Larsson, Bozena Werbart, Karin Viklund, and P. Ajithprasad.

Ellen M. Raven is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. She held positions at Leiden University, attested in 2003 and 2018, and served on the editorial board of Gonda Indological Studies (attested 2018).
Elliot M. Stern is an Indologist. He earned his doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania under George Cardona and Wilhelm Halbfass, and also studied under P. N. Pattabhirama Sastri.

Elliot Sperling was a scholar of Tibetology, sinology, and history. He completed his MA and PhD at Indiana University Bloomington under Helmut Hoffmann and Thubten Jigme Norbu, and taught at Indiana University Bloomington as associate professor (1987–2015).
